<issue>
ADD COLUMN + RENAME TABLE in one transaction corrupts catalog metadata ("Column with name ... already exists!" on every read)
### What happens?

`ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` followed by `ALTER TABLE ... RENAME TO` in the same transaction commits successfully but writes corrupt catalog metadata. Every subsequent read of the table — from any connection, including a fresh `ATTACH` — fails with:

```
Catalog Error: Column with name id already exists!
```

After the commit, the metadata catalog contains two live rows in `ducklake_table` for the same `table_id` (the pre-rename row's `end_snapshot` is never set alongside the new row), and the added column is never written to `ducklake_column` at all. Catalog load reads the table twice and hits the duplicate-column error.

No data is involved — the table can be empty. Either ALTER alone is fine; only the combination corrupts. ADD COLUMN + RENAME **COLUMN** (as opposed to renaming the table) is also fine without inlining, so this is distinct from #740.

This looks like another instance of the two-ALTERs-in-one-transaction family: same symptom as #683, which #714 fixed for the ALTER TYPE + SET DEFAULT pair; the repro below still fails on current `main`, which contains #714. Also adjacent: #973 (SET DEFAULT + RENAME, closed) and #740 (ADD + RENAME COLUMN with inlined-data flush, open — different failure: its catalog stays intact and the inlined-data read path breaks instead).

Found via PR #1306's CI: DuckDB's `test/sql/transactions/test_ddl_after_dml.test` under `test/configs/attach_ducklake.json` previously self-skipped (an earlier statement hit the whitelisted non-literal default error); that PR makes the statement succeed, so the test now runs far enough to hit this bug at its `restart`.

### To Reproduce

```sql
ATTACH 'ducklake:x.db' AS dl; USE dl;
CREATE TABLE t2 (id INT);
BEGIN;
ALTER TABLE t2 ADD COLUMN c0 INT DEFAULT 7;
ALTER TABLE t2 RENAME TO t3;
COMMIT;
SELECT * FROM t3;    -- Catalog Error: Column with name id already exists!
```

The COMMIT succeeds; the SELECT fails, and so does any later `ATTACH` + read from a new process. The broken metadata is visible directly:

```sql
ATTACH 'x.db' AS meta;
SELECT table_id, begin_snapshot, end_snapshot, table_name FROM meta.ducklake_table;
-- table_id 1 | begin 1 | end NULL | t2     <- never closed
-- table_id 1 | begin 2 | end NULL | t3
SELECT column_id, column_name FROM meta.ducklake_column;
-- only "id" — the added column c0 was never written
```

### OS:

Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm), kernel 6.1.0-44-amd64, x86_64

### DuckDB Version:

duckdb `main` (source build) @ `0cd9e82950` (`v1.5.3-7258-g0cd9e82950`)

### DuckLake Version:

ducklake `main` @ `34db89b27efe23a2037df83bf809720cad64d915`

### DuckDB Client:

CLI

### Hardware:

Not performance-related.

### Full Name:

Gavin Brand

### Affiliation:

N/A

### What is the latest build you tested with? If possible, we recommend testing with the latest nightly build.

I have tested with a source build

### Did you include all relevant data sets for reproducing the issue?

Not applicable - the reproduction does not require a data set

### Did you include all code required to reproduce the issue?

- [X] Yes, I have

### Did you include all relevant configuration (e.g., CPU architecture, Python version, Linux distribution) to reproduce the issue?

- [X] Yes, I have


</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.

input.instruction: In /testbed (DuckLake), find in src/ the code handling transaction commit of altered tables (ducklake_transaction.cc): functions dealing with altered_tables, new_tables, renamed tables, added columns (e.g. GetTableChanges, CommitChanges, GetNewTables, "AddedColumn", "new_columns"), and the earlier fix for ALTER TYPE + SET DEFAULT (#714) in the same transaction. Report the relevant code with line numbers and how a table that is both in new_tables (from rename -> new table entry) and has added columns is handled.

content.content: {"summary":"The commit logic is in src/storage/ducklake_transaction_state.cpp, not ducklake_transaction.cpp (there is no .cc file). ducklake_transaction.cpp has the helpers and the alter entry points. For a table in new_tables with added columns, GetNewTableInfo walks the alter chain oldest to newest. It emits the table row (RENAMED/CREATED case) plus separate new_columns entries. I found no explicit '#714' marker in the code. The ALTER TYPE + SET DEFAULT fix appears to be the txn_added_fields / CancelOrDropField mechanism. I did not run or test anything.","findings":["ducklake_transaction.cpp:762: GetNewTables() returns state->new_tables. ducklake_transaction.cpp:959-1010 builds TransactionChangeInformation from new_tables via GetTransactionTableChanges/ViewChanges. ducklake_transaction.cpp:682: LocalTableChangeIteratorEntry::GetTableChanges.","ducklake_transaction.cpp:1178-1197: GetNewTable() keeps the existing id for a non-local table (e.g. a rename). For a transaction-local table it allocates a new id from next_catalog_id++. It writes table.GetTableColumns() only when the table is new (is_new_table). A renamed existing table therefore gets a new_tables row with no columns, and its column changes are emitted separately.","ducklake_transaction.cpp:1993-2020: AlterEntryInternal(table) puts the new entry into the transaction-local entries. For RENAMED it calls HandleRenameOldEntry, which records renamed_tables or dropped_tables. ADD_COLUMN, SET_DEFAULT, CHANGE_COLUMN_TYPE and the other alter types are only added to the chain.","ducklake_transaction_state.cpp:1180-1224: GetNewTableInfo gathers the table's entry chain (newest is the root) and counts alters per field (field_alter_count) for SET_NULL, DROP_NULL, RENAME_COLUMN and SET_DEFAULT. It also counts comments.","ducklake_transaction_state.cpp:1225-1340: the chain is processed in reverse, oldest first. A txn_added_fields map (field_id to index in result.new_columns) tracks columns added in this transaction. ADD_COLUMN (1301-1311) pushes a DuckLakeNewColumn with table.GetAddColumnInfo(), registers it in txn_added_fields, and marks altered_tables and altered_tables_with_schema_version_changes.","ducklake_transaction_state.cpp:1271-1296: SET_NULL, DROP_NULL, RENAME_COLUMN and SET_DEFAULT. Older superseded alters of the same field are skipped (field_alter_remaining > 0). The newest alter calls CancelOrDropField and then pushes a new column with table.GetColumnInfo(field). This is the likely mechanism for ALTER TYPE + SET DEFAULT in one transaction.","ducklake_transaction_state.cpp:1312-1319: REMOVE_COLUMN and CHANGE_COLUMN_TYPE call HandleChangedFields (state.cpp:~425-450). It runs CancelOrDropField for each dropped field, then adds new_fields columns and registers them in txn_added_fields. CancelOrDropField (state.cpp:~408-428) erases the pending new_columns entry if the field was added in this transaction, and fixes the indexes of the other entries. Otherwise it emits a dropped_columns entry.","ducklake_transaction_state.cpp:1345-1372: the NONE/CREATED/RENAMED case. If the table was renamed after being created in the same transaction (IsTransactionLocal(old_id) and already in commit_state.committed_tables), RenameEmittedEntry patches the name of the already-emitted new_tables entry and breaks, so there is no duplicate row. Otherwise GetNewTable is called and the row is pushed to result.new_tables. The old-to-new id is recorded in commit_state.committed_tables. An inlined-data table entry is also created from tables.front() (the latest schema, with all alters applied).","Table in new_tables with added columns: the ids are remapped through commit_state.GetTableId(table). For a created table, the full latest column set is written by GetNewTable via GetTableColumns(). The ADD_COLUMN entries in the chain still push new_columns for the same table id, with txn_added_fields tracking them. For a rename of an existing table, the new_tables row has no columns, and the added columns go in as new_columns rows against the same id. I did not find any dedup of added columns against GetTableColumns() for a created table. I did not trace it further.","ducklake_transaction_state.cpp:1511-1525 (GetNewTables) iterates state->new_tables and calls GetNewTableInfo. ducklake_transaction_state.cpp:1566 and 1605-1631 drop renamed_tables, call WriteNewTables, and write result.new_columns (1628). ducklake_transaction_state.cpp:1756-1764 uses altered_tables_with_schema_version_changes and the new_tables_result ids."],"confidence":0.6}

input.instruction: In /testbed/src, show code for HandleRenameOldEntry and how renamed_tables / dropped_tables get populated, and the AlterEntryInternal(table) function in ducklake_transaction.cpp (full bodies with line numbers), plus where ADD COLUMN alter is handled in ducklake_table_entry.cpp / ducklake_transaction.cpp (what sets local change / how entries are placed in the new_tables set when the table is not transaction-local).

content.content: {"summary":"I traced the rename, drop and alter paths in ducklake_transaction.cpp and the ADD COLUMN path in ducklake_table_entry.cpp. I did not print full function bodies with line numbers as the job asked, only line ranges and short quotes. ADD COLUMN has no placement logic of its own. It builds a new entry with LocalChangeType::ADD_COLUMN. AlterEntryInternal then inserts that entry into the transaction-local new_tables set, which is created on demand.","findings":["HandleRenameOldEntry is a static function at ducklake_transaction.cpp:1992-2011. It has three branches. (1) If IsTransactionLocal(id) is true, the table was created in this transaction. It drops old_name from the entries set and attaches the dropped entry as a child of the new entry via SetChild. (2) Otherwise, if entry_is_transaction_local is true, the committed table was already altered earlier in this transaction. It only calls entries.DropEntry(old_name). (3) Otherwise this is the first rename of a committed entry. It asserts the id is not in dropped_set, then runs renamed_set.insert(id).","renamed_tables is a set<TableIndex> declared at include/storage/ducklake_transaction_state.hpp:210. It is populated only through HandleRenameOldEntry's third branch, called from AlterEntryInternal(table) at ducklake_transaction.cpp:2019-2021. DropTable erases the id from it at line 1822. At commit, ducklake_transaction_state.cpp:1566-1567 calls DropTables(renamed_tables, true).","dropped_tables is a set<TableIndex> declared at ducklake_transaction_state.hpp:203. It is populated only in DuckLakeTransaction::DropTable, at ducklake_transaction.cpp:1820-1824. That code runs `if (!IsTransactionLocal(table_id.index)) { state->renamed_tables.erase(table_id); state->dropped_tables.insert(table_id); }`. For a table created in this transaction, DropTable instead removes it from new_tables and cleans up its files (lines 1805-1818). At commit, ducklake_transaction_state.cpp:1562-1563 calls DropTables(dropped_tables, false).","AlterEntryInternal(DuckLakeTableEntry&, unique_ptr<CatalogEntry>) is at ducklake_transaction.cpp:2013-2039. It casts new_entry to DuckLakeTableEntry, then calls GetOrCreateTransactionLocalEntries(table) and entries.CreateEntry(std::move(new_entry)). It then switches on new_table.GetLocalChange().type. The RENAMED case calls HandleRenameOldEntry with table.name, new_table.name, table.GetTableId(), table.IsTransactionLocal(), state->renamed_tables and state->dropped_tables. The cases ADD_COLUMN, SET_PARTITION_KEY, SET_COMMENT, SET_COLUMN_COMMENT, SET_NULL, DROP_NULL, RENAME_COLUMN, REMOVE_COLUMN, CHANGE_COLUMN_TYPE, SET_DEFAULT and SET_SORT_KEY just break. Any other type throws NotImplementedException.","AlterEntry at ducklake_transaction.cpp:~1975-1989 sets catalog_version = GetNewUncommittedCatalogVersion(). It returns early if new_entry is null. It then dispatches to the table overload for TABLE_ENTRY or the view overload (line 2041) for VIEW_ENTRY.","GetOrCreateTransactionLocalEntries is at ducklake_transaction.cpp:2059-2092. For tables and views it looks up state->new_tables by schema name. If there is no entry, it creates a new DuckLakeCatalogSet and runs `new_tables.insert(make_pair(schema_name, std::move(new_table_list)))`. This is how an altered committed table ends up in new_tables.","ADD COLUMN is handled in DuckLakeTableEntry::AlterTable(..., AddColumnInfo&) at ducklake_table_entry.cpp:778-826. It rejects reserved inlined system column names when inlining is enabled. It returns nullptr if if_column_not_exists is set and the column exists. It then runs table_info.columns.AddColumn(...), RequireNextColumnId(transaction), and `make_uniq<DuckLakeTableEntry>(*this, table_info, LocalChangeType::ADD_COLUMN)` at line 799. If the transaction has inlined data for the table, it calls transaction.AddColumnToLocalInlinedData(...) at line 818.","The local change is set by the DuckLakeTableEntry copy constructor (ducklake_table_entry.cpp:136-158). It forwards the LocalChange to the main constructor (lines 103-110), which stores it as the local_change member. In the ADD_COLUMN branch (lines 147-152) it updates field_data via DuckLakeFieldData::AddColumn and then next_column_id.","DuckLakeTableEntry::IsTransactionLocal() at include/storage/ducklake_table_entry.hpp:51 returns `local_change.type != LocalChangeType::NONE`. Any altered entry therefore counts as transaction-local. This separates HandleRenameOldEntry's branch 2 from branch 3. The free function IsTransactionLocal(TableIndex) is a different check, used for tables created in this transaction."],"confidence":0.8}
